### Data

All-cause mortality counts and population exposure estimates, disaggregated by sex and single year of age and period, were obtained from the Human Mortality Database [@hmd2024] for Northern Ireland (`GBR_NIR`). Comparator populations include Scotland (`GBR_SCO`), England and Wales (`GBRTENW`), the Republic of Ireland (`IRL`), and a composite of Western European nations.

All data management and analyses were performed using R [@rcoreteam2024]. Code to reproduce all analyses is available at <https://github.com/JonMinton/shape-of-the-troubles>.

### Visual exploration

Mortality rates were calculated by dividing death counts by population exposure. These rates were then visualised as Lexis surfaces — heatmaps in which each column represents a year, each row an age, and cell colour indicates the log~10~ mortality rate [@minton2014; @vaupel1997].

### The initiation-decay model

```{r}
#| label: fig-impulse-decay-schematic
#| fig-cap: "Schematic of the impulse-decay model for conflict intensity"
#| eval: false

# TODO: Generate schematic of T(t) parameter
```

The Troubles parameter $T(t)$ operationalises the hypothesis that conflict followed a single impulse-decay pattern, with events prior to 1972 leading to a tipping point, after which sectarian violence was sustained through tit-for-tat reprisals but gradually attenuated.

Formally:

$$
T(t) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } t < 1972 \\ (1-k)^{t-1972} & \text{if } t \geq 1972 \end{cases}
$$

where $k$ is the annual decay rate. The half-life of conflict intensity is $h = \ln(0.5) / \ln(1-k)$.

### Model specification

The full model for log~10~ mortality rate in males aged 15--45 is:

$$
\log_{10}(\mu_{a,t}) = f(a) + g^{(p)}(a, t) + \beta_a \cdot T(t) + \epsilon_{a,t}
$$

where $f(a)$ captures age-specific baseline mortality, $g^{(p)}(a, t)$ captures age-specific mortality improvement within phase $p$, and $\beta_a \cdot T(t)$ captures the age-specific effect of the Troubles.

Three mortality improvement phases were identified through visual exploration:

- **Phase 1** (1922--1938): Pre-war baseline
- **Phase 2** (1939--1955): Rapid improvement (despite including WWII)
- **Phase 3** (1956 onwards): Continued but slower improvement

The decay rate $k$ was selected to minimise AIC through numerical optimisation.

### Counterfactual estimation

Excess deaths attributable to the Troubles were estimated by comparing predicted deaths under the fitted model with predictions from a counterfactual model in which $T(t) = 0$ for all years.
